title: Secretary of State of Indiana

context.text: The seat is open. Incumbent Diego Morales (R) lost the June 20 Republican convention to Max Engling after U.S. Sen. Jim Banks and Attorney General Todd Rokita pulled their endorsements of Morales; Republicans have held the office since 1994.

Indiana nominates its Secretary of State at party conventions. Beau Bayh defeated Blythe Potter at the June 6 Democratic convention; Greg Ballard qualified as the Lincoln Party candidate, a new party, and the Libertarian Party nominated Lauri Shillings.
Ballotpedia designates the race a battleground and says Bayh, Engling and Ballard lead in media attention and fundraising.

The Indiana Election Division's September 22, 2026 candidate list shows Bayh (Democratic), Engling (Republican), Ballard (Lincoln Party) and Shillings (Libertarian) for Secretary of State, plus a write-in filing by Andrew Delano (National Socialist American Workers').
Ballard's ballot access was confirmed by Election Division staff on July 22, 2026, after he submitted more than 70,000 petition signatures.

candidates.name: Beau Bayh
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 6 Democratic convention over Blythe Potter.

priorities.text: Fix what he calls a corrupt office: he supports an audit of the Secretary of State's office and said at the Oct. 7 debate he would start a forensic audit of current spending.
Election security and access: 'No illegal votes, period. But we also should make sure that eligible voters can participate in our democracy.'

positions.summary: Told the Indiana Capital Chronicle he supports Indiana's ban on transgender girls in girls' school sports, calling it a nonissue for the office.
positions.quote: I think we should not have men playing women's sports, and our state has already passed a law outlawing this

candidates.researchNotes: Has never held office, so no record. Campaign site (beaubayh.com) returned a block page. Said at the Aug. 26 debate that votes in a disputed state Senate recount should be counted absent evidence of fraud; he did not state a view on the SAVE America Act in the sources reviewed; at the Oct. 7 debate he said he supports Indiana's current voter ID law.

candidates.name: Max Engling
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 20 Republican convention over David Shelton, incumbent Diego Morales and Jamie Reitenour (Morales received 8.2% of delegate votes).

priorities.text: Election reforms, including 'ensuring that only citizens can vote in Indiana elections' and 'closing primaries to prevent crossover voting,' per his campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia News.
Improve oversight and monitoring of business fraud and reduce regulatory burdens on business filings.
Create a transparency portal for citizens to report potential election issues directly, per his campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia News.

positions.summary: Said on WIBC that boys should not play in girls' sports; his campaign chairman also criticized opponent Greg Ballard over the topic, though the office has no role in it.
positions.quote: we have to protect our girls and women in sports, and boys should not be playing in their sports.

candidates.researchNotes: Has not held elected office; no record to list. Was the only candidate who did not pledge an audit of the office, per the Capital Chronicle; at the Oct. 7 debate he backed a review by the state inspector general instead. His campaign site was not located, so campaign-site language is as quoted by Ballotpedia News.

statements.quote: It’s also important that we have only eligible citizens voting in our elections.
statements.context: At the Aug. 26 debate, where the Capital Chronicle reported he was the only candidate to support the full federal SAVE America Act; he did not describe the act's documentary-proof requirement in this remark.

candidates.name: Greg Ballard
candidates.ballotNote: On the ballot as the Lincoln Party candidate after petitioning: the Election Division staff verified 40,361 signatures against a 36,943 requirement.

priorities.text: Restore stability and dignity to the office, with an audit that emphasizes travel expenses.
Mail a paper voter guide to every registered voter, backed by a software app, at a cost the Capital Chronicle puts at up to $2.5 million per election cycle.
Make it easier for independents to run: he says his party offers 'hope to people who actually want to run for office without punitive signature requirements.'

positions.summary: Said boys do not belong in girls' sports or locker rooms, but also called Indiana's 2022 ban 'unnecessary' and stood by supporting then-Gov. Holcomb's veto of it, saying sports organizations were handling the issue.
positions.quote: boys don’t belong in girls’ sports nor in their locker rooms.

record.text: Served as Mayor of Indianapolis from 2008 to 2016.

candidates.researchNotes: The signature count (40,361 verified; more than 70,000 reported collected) is from the Indiana Capital Chronicle and Election Division staff. At the Aug. 26 debate he said Indiana's election security record is solid and called the SAVE America Act a federal intrusion (Capital Chronicle's paraphrase); no verbatim quote on documentary proof of citizenship was found, so no position is listed for that issue. Ballotpedia's summary also lists him as an independent.

candidates.name: Lauri Shillings

priorities.text: Neutral leadership: the office should operate independently, professionally and without partisan agenda.
Competence: make elections, business filings and state records systems efficient, accurate and easy to navigate.
Accountability: transparency in spending and openness to oversight; she supports an audit of the office.

positions.summary: Called the SAVE America Act a barrier to voting at the Aug. 26 debate.
positions.quote: I believe that it disenfranchises people who absolutely should be able to vote.

candidates.researchNotes: Depth limited to her survey, the debate coverage and Ballotpedia; no campaign website was located.

researchNotes: Slate confirmed on the Indiana Election Division's candidate list dated Sept. 22, 2026 (four candidates plus write-in Andrew Delano, National Socialist American Workers', whom this guide does not profile because no campaign materials were found). Ballotpedia (blocked by an automated challenge) could not be re-read, so details sourced only to it were not re-verified. Indiana has no Attorney General election in 2026 (Rokita was elected in 2024), so there is no in-ag file.
